title: What architecture is not: neither a pretty diagram nor the fashionable technology

videos.script: Three things are often mistaken for architecture, and this lesson takes them away one at a time. {{title}} The first is the diagram. Carreto shows every new engineer the same slide, drawn in 2021. Renata checks it against the running system, and finds a gateway that was never built and five connections nobody drew. {{slide}} A diagram is a view. The architecture is what the system actually does. {{view}} The second is the technology. An engineer proposes moving Carreto to microservices, because everyone does. Renata asks a different question. Which problem does it solve, and what does it cost? {{proposal}} Tools follow from the qualities a system needs, not the other way round. {{chain}} The third is the idea that architecture is a phase. Either all of it is decided at the start, or none of it is decided at all. Both fail. {{phase}} Some decisions have a moment, and waiting past it means the code decides for you. Others are better left until the team knows more. {{moment}} By the end you should be able to tell a decision that must be made now from one that can wait.
